_note: Names dropped by hand from every list, each with its reason. Ordinary words that are also given names are KEPT (a missed name is the worse mistake); a name goes here only when it does real harm as a gate in a header such as 'Plan for X Y'. Keys are lower case; one object per language, applied to that language's list.

en.baby: Ontario's registrations hold "Baby" for an unnamed newborn (22,709 births): a placeholder, not a name, and an everyday care word
en.female: a care word ("Screening for Female Patients"), not a name
en.male: a care word ("Screening for Male Patients"), not a name
en.infant: a care word ("Care plan for Infant Feeding"), not a name
en.walker: a mobility aid ("Assessment for Walker Use")
en.ward: a hospital ward ("Plan for Ward Round")
en.not: an ordinary word that registrations hold as a rare name
en.real: an ordinary word that registrations hold as a rare name
en.line: "line management", "line change"; the French name Line stays in the French list

fr.elder: an English care word ("elder care") held as a rare name
fr.junior: an English word held as a rare name (a suffix of a name, not a name)

pl.inna: an ordinary Polish word ("another"); documented false positive in pasteBackForms.test.ts
